text:
Tristan Luneau had played 15 NHL games before this season. Twenty games in, the 22-year-old is playing 20 minutes a night on the Ducks' blue line and has 14 points, 12 of them in his last ten, a run that included an eight-game point streak and a long-range power-play goal against Pittsburgh.

Our form check calls the hot streak earned, which is unusual for a young defenseman scoring this much. He's getting more and better shots than his usual rate, and Anaheim takes 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, 15 points better than without him, the biggest gap on the team. That's not a passenger.

Some caution belongs here. Four goals on 1.6 expected won't hold, his minutes dipped about two a night over the last ten, and the only Evolving-Hockey season on file (125 minutes in 2023-24) had him struggling defensively. The second-round pick from Gatineau put up 83 points in his last junior season. The question now is whether this is the start of a top-four career or a hot month, and so far the process says the former.
